transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-02
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Sofia Morales (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Neill (BlueArc Lead NetOps), Priya Reddy (BlueArc SRE), Jonas Müller (BlueArc Platform), Emma Zhao (BlueArc Security), Tom Baker (BlueArc Product)

Summary:
Quick status sync on the private pilot (VPC + on-prem connector). Main topics: recent kernel regression causing tail latency spikes, connectivity handshake flakiness between BlueArc's egress gateway and Redwood's private nodes, and the rollforward plan for canarying the fix. We agreed on a short test plan and a tentative canary window next Thursday. Action items assigned.

Topics:
- Kernel regression and rollback options
- Handshake/PSK failures and retransmit behavior
- Telemetry gaps (trace ids missing for some flows)
- Security/compliance checks (KMS, audit logs)
- Canary schedule and traffic replay for validation

Action items (recap): Marcus to deploy hotfix staging, Liam to share traffic capture, Sofia to send pricing and next steps, Emma to confirm KMS policy.

Transcript:
00:00 Avery Chen: okay everyone uh thanks for joining, I think we can go ahead and get started, we've got about 45 minutes today so we'll try to be focused
00:12 Liam O'Neill: awesome thanks Avery, and quick note there's a new person on my side Jonas who's been pulled in for the platform details so hi Jonas
00:19 Jonas Müller: hey all, yeah thanks, been through the earlier emails about the handshake errors
00:25 Marcus Patel: right, so quick TL;DR, we pushed kernel 0.9.2 last week to the private nodes, and we saw an unexpected tail latency increase around the 99.9th percentile, looks correlated to larger sequence lengths and the new KV cache path
00:40 Priya Reddy: yes correct, our profiling shows a spike when sequence > 4k tokens, which is not common but in our batch replays it shows up during long doc summarization jobs
00:51 Avery Chen: okay, and the KV cache you mean the K-V cash path? (laughs) the auto-transcribe always does that, but yeah the prefix/k-v cache handling is changed in 0.9.2
01:02 Liam O'Neill: also we're seeing intermittent handshake timeouts between our egress gateway and your private nodes, roughly 1 in 2,000 requests fail with a timeout, not a TLS cert issue, looks like retransmit backpressure
01:18 Marcus Patel: that's the big one we wanted to surface. There's a race in the connection reuse logic when a partial prefix is cached locally; the runtime drops the request and the client retries which causes a small burst and the node's accept queue spikes
01:33 Tom Baker: can you explain in plain terms, is this an app-level retry or something in the infra? Product team needs to understand operational risk
01:41 Marcus Patel: good question, it's infra-level; if the node hasn't fully reconstructed the KV context the runtime reports an error and the client library triggers the default retry policy (which BlueArc has at 3 attempts), so it's retry amplification in a narrow window
01:56 Emma Zhao: from a security perspective any retry window that amplifies requests is concerning, we also noted some missing audit ids in about 0.3% of the flows in our logs
02:06 Avery Chen: right, telemetry gap — thanks for flagging Emma. That might be related to the same race; the trace id is attached after certain handshake steps so if the request is short-circuited it never gets stamped
02:18 Liam O'Neill: timeline wise, how quick can Redwood push a fix? We have a business-critical demo the week after next so we need stability this week for staging
02:29 Marcus Patel: we can prepare a hotfix kernel 0.9.3 that backports the previous KV handling and adds a defensive accept-queue cap. My ask would be to run it in staging with a production-like replay for 24 hours
02:41 Priya Reddy: we can run that replay, we'll need a plan for safe rollback if our consumers see errors
02:49 Marcus Patel: rollback will be immediate — the runtime flags allow safe downgrade without restarting the whole pool, it's a config flip essentially
02:58 Jonas Müller: what about the handshake flakiness — is that going to be addressed in 0.9.3 or is that separate?
03:06 Marcus Patel: related but separate — the hotfix includes a more conservative connection reuse policy, it should drop the rate of timeouts by ~80% in our testing, but for full certificate/tls renegotiation edge cases we'll have a follow up patch
03:18 Avery Chen: ok, so short term fix 0.9.3 addresses the accept queue and connection reuse conservative defaults; follow-up for TLS edgecases after we validate
03:26 Liam O'Neill: good. about telemetry, if trace ids get dropped what's the visibility impact for our SREs? we rely on per-request tracing for SLA validation
03:36 Sofia Morales: we should take that seriously — Emma, do you have a list of the missing fields you saw?
03:41 Emma Zhao: yes, missing trace_id and sometimes user_agent header, both observed in the same subset; I'll share a sample in the channel, looks like ~0.3% of requests across two days
03:50 Priya Reddy: ok we'll correlate with our side logs, maybe the ingress strip is happening on our egress gateway, we'll rule that out first
03:58 Tom Baker: another question, how does this affect cost — if retries spike we could see billing anomalies, will Redwood be able to suppress billing for spike retries during the pilot?
04:09 Avery Chen: we can do a play — for the pilot we offered a pro-rated adjustment for retry amplification events, we can open a ticket to reconcile billing once we have captures
04:20 Liam O'Neill: yes please, we'd like that reconciliation as part of the next steps
04:24 Marcus Patel: also practical note, for the staging run we'll need the traffic replay and a short list of representative prompt lengths and concurrency patterns, otherwise the 4k token edge won't appear
04:35 Priya Reddy: I'll add that to the export, we've got a job that can replay by token length buckets
04:40 Avery Chen: perfect. next, networking — we found a pattern where MTU blackhole can create partial frames that look like handshake failures; can you confirm MTU between your egress and our interconnect?
04:51 Liam O'Neill: our egress is 1500, we have jumbo frames enabled on the internal path, but there's a firewall in between managed by a partner that could be doing MSS clamping, we'll check with them
05:03 Jonas Müller: we could instrument an MTU pathcheck during the staging run, that might be quick to rule out
05:09 Marcus Patel: yes please, we also recommend disabling TCP offload on the gateway for the test window — it can change timing behavior and mask the real issue
05:17 Priya Reddy: noted, we'll disable offload for the replay host
05:21 Avery Chen: on the security/compliance side — Emma you flagged KMS rotation questions, what do you need from us?
05:28 Emma Zhao: primarily the key policy and rotation cadence, also whether Redwood keeps any plaintext logs in the private control plane during the handshake
05:36 Marcus Patel: we don't keep plaintext tokens in the control plane, only encrypted blobs; we'll share the architecture diagram and the control-plane retention policy in the docs bundle
05:44 Emma Zhao: okay if you can attach the SOC2 excerpt showing encryption-at-rest and KMS integration that would be ideal
05:50 Sofia Morales: I will attach a compliance pack after the call, including SOC2 excerpt, KMS integration notes, and audit log format samples
05:58 Liam O'Neill: back to the canary plan — what's the proposal for traffic shaping and fallback if we see a regression during canary?
06:06 Marcus Patel: proposal: start with 1% of production traffic using a shadow routing policy, then if metrics look good ramp to 10% over two hours; automatic fallback policy will re-route to the previous model variant and pin capacity while we investigate
06:20 Priya Reddy: how fast is fallback? we need sub-minute rollback to meet SLA requirements
06:26 Marcus Patel: fallback is immediate — routing policy is controller-driven and will divert new requests at the gateway level; in-flight requests may finish but new ones won't land on the canary nodes
06:36 Tom Baker: and how will we measure user-impact during canary? what metrics?
06:42 Avery Chen: we'll track 99/99.9 latency, error rate, and also token-level cost delta; plus a sampling of actual generated outputs to validate quality regressions
06:51 Jonas Müller: for output quality sampling can we integrate with BlueArc's eval harness? we have a small automation that runs prompt sets and scores freshness and hallucination metrics
06:59 Marcus Patel: yes we can run that hook and surface failed prompts as alerts in the Redwood Console runbook
07:06 Liam O'Neill: schedule wise, you said next Thursday for a canary? that's 2026-07-09, is that still doable for Redwood?
07:13 Marcus Patel: yes but contingent on getting the replay by Monday and us completing the staging run by Wednesday, that gives us a window for fixes
07:21 Priya Reddy: one more operational ask: during the staging run we want an expanded telemetry retention so we can deep-dive traces — can Redwood temporarily increase retention for the pilot artifacts?
07:31 Avery Chen: we can extend retention for pilot artifacts for a short window, we'll scope that in the ticket, it's not an issue
07:36 Emma Zhao: also please include audit log format so we can validate compliance ingestion into our SIEM
07:41 Sofia Morales: yes included in the compliance pack I'll share
07:45 Liam O'Neill: curious, have you seen comparable regressions in other customers after 0.9.2, or is this unique to our workload?
07:53 Marcus Patel: we've seen one other partner with long sequence loads see a smaller 99.9 spike, but the handshake timeouts were unique to your particular egress topology — likely an interplay between MSS clamping and offload settings
08:04 Tom Baker: so what are our milestones this week? can you summarize?
08:09 Avery Chen: sure — 1) Marcus pushes 0.9.3 to staging by Monday, 2) BlueArc provides traffic replay and MTU checks by Monday, 3) staging run and validation completed by Wednesday, 4) canary window Thursday 2026-07-09, 5) billing reconciliation ticket opened if retry amplification observed
08:27 Liam O'Neill: that works. also we have one procurement question — if we go to Dedicated after pilot, what's the lead time for reserved capacity?
08:35 Sofia Morales: typically 4-6 weeks for Dedicated capacity provisioned through the reserved contract, shorter if we can reuse spots in the same region; I'll include this in the pricing doc
08:43 Jonas Müller: quick technical follow-up — Marcus mentioned safe downgrade config flip. does that require draining nodes or is it zero-downtime?
08:51 Marcus Patel: it's zero-downtime for new connections, we avoid draining but we do recommend a short maintenance window to clear existing KV contexts, otherwise you might observe a transient spike while caches reconcile
09:03 Priya Reddy: that makes sense, we'll accept a 5-10 minute maintenance window if recommended
09:09 Avery Chen: ok, last housekeeping — Emma, you'll get the SOC2 excerpt, Sofia will share pricing, Marcus will drop the hotfix and results, Liam will share the replay. Anything else?
09:20 Emma Zhao: one tiny ask — can we get an ephemeral test KMS key to validate rotation end-to-end in staging?
09:27 Marcus Patel: yes we can create a test key and scope it to the staging control plane, we'll note that in the ticket
09:33 Liam O'Neill: great thanks everyone, that was efficient.
09:37 Avery Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up in the pilot channel and confirm the Monday drop, see you in the canary planning sync next week
09:44 (call ends)
